title: Acceptance characterized by the bounded-run answer
statement: Let $c$ be a machine-representation scheme, and let $\alpha,x$ be binary strings and $t\in\mathbb{N}$. Run the machine decoded from $\alpha$ on $x$ for $t$ steps, and form the answer word by prefixing its output with $1$ if it has halted by then, or by taking the one-bit word $0$ if it has not halted. This answer word is $11$ if and only if the decoded machine computes the one-bit output $1$ from $x$ within $t$ steps.
replaced: Let $c$ be a machine-representation scheme, which assigns to every bit string $\alpha$ a one-work-tape binary Turing machine $M_\alpha$ (decoding is total). For all bit strings $\alpha, x$ and $t \in \mathbb{N}$, let $A_c(\alpha,x,t)$ be $1w$ if $M_\alpha$ run on $x$ for $t$ steps has halted with output $w$, and the single bit $0$ otherwise. Then $A_c(\alpha,x,t) = 11$ if and only if $M_\alpha$ on input $x$ halts within $t$ steps with output exactly the single bit $1$.
